newsitem.title: USA: Ashland Inc to sell Blazer to Statoil unit.
newsitem.headline: Ashland Inc to sell Blazer to Statoil unit.

text.p: Ashland Inc said on Wednesday it signed a definitive agreement to sell its Blazer Energy Corp subsidiary to Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap A/S (Statoil) of Norway for $566 million in cash.
The deal, which includes virtually all of Ashland's domestic oil and natural gas properties , will be made through Statoil's U.S. subsidiary, the Eastern Group Inc.
If approved by regulators and Statoil's supervisory board, the deal is expected to close by July 1, Ashland said said in a news release.
Statoil said Blazer's Appalachian Basin properties will be retained by Eastern, while its Gulf of Mexico properties will be operated by Statoil Exploration (U.S.) Inc.
Privately-held Eastern Group is 83 percent owned by Statoil.
Reuters reported earlier that Ashland chief executive Paul Chellgren had characterized the sale as "highly likely", with sources familiar to talks identifying Eastern as the potential buyer.
Ashland is a Kentucky-based energy and chemical company engaged in petroleum refining and marketing, coal and highway construction.

Ashland said it has not yet developed a specific plan for the proceeds of the sale, but noted it has the potential to reduce debt and accelerate investment in growth areas. The company plans to focus on its chemicals business, APAC highway construction group and Valvoline motor oil operations.
The company also said Statoil has indicated it hopes to retain a large number of Blazer workers. The unit has about 300 employees.
